ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.label: beekeepers
ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.leavesWhy: beekeepers carry their hives with them to the next flowering ground

texts.li: A beekeeping family of {FACTION} has come along the road with their hives roped to a pack beast, following the flowers. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} the colony's land is in bloom, and asked to camp {PLACE} for a few days and let the bees work it.

[their:tribal] Honey-gatherers of {FACTION} have come with their hives slung on poles and a beast to carry the rest. {X_nameDef} said the flowers here called their bees, and asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} until the bloom is over.

[their:medieval] A beekeeper of {FACTION} and the family have come up the track with their hives and a pack beast that walks very carefully. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for leave to set the hives {PLACE} while the flowers last. They will sell honey and wax, {X_pronoun} says, and keep the bees to themselves.

[their:industrial] An apiarist of {FACTION} has brought a wagon of hives and a family to work them. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} for a week of the colony's flowers, and sell honey at the stall in return.

settled.li: The beekeepers' camp {PLACE} is up. Their hives stand at the edge of it with the bees already out over the colony's flowers, and their stall smells of honey.
The beekeepers from {FACTION} have made camp {PLACE}, with the hives set at the far side from the fire so the smoke stays off them.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the beekeepers {PLACE}, says the bees like it here better than anywhere on the road, and asks whether the colony would like someone who knows them to stay.
{X_nameDef} of the beekeepers camped {PLACE} says the colony's flowers would keep a hive or two busy all summer, and asks whether there is a place here for someone to keep them.

farewell.li: The beekeepers from {FACTION} have roped their hives back onto the pack beast and gone on after the flowers.
The beekeepers' camp {PLACE} is empty. The bees went with them, mostly.
[back] The beekeepers who came before have gone on again, and {X_nameDef} says the bees will want to come back next summer.

lines.li: Move slowly near the hives.
They're on the clover today.
Smoke them first, then lift the lid.
That's a good heavy frame.
Don't swat it, it'll call the others.
The queen's laying well.
Never take the last of their honey.
[rain] They won't fly in this.
[their:tribal] The bees know whose hand it is.
[their:industrial] The frames are full, we'll spin them tonight.

helpTexts.li: [mend] {X_nameDef} of the beekeepers saw how worn {A_nameDef}'s {THING} was and mended it there and then, the way {X_pronoun} mends the hive cloths.

li.label: Buy a crock of their honey ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: One of the beekeepers carries a crock of honey to the colony's gate.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} took the silver and filled a crock from the best of the frames. One of them is carrying it over to the colony's gate.
The beekeepers will carry a crock of honey over to the colony's gate today, wrapped in a cloth against the flies.

li.label: Buy their beeswax ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: One of the beekeepers carries a bundle of beeswax to the colony's gate.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} took the silver and wrapped the wax in a leaf. One of the beekeepers is carrying it over to the colony's gate.

li.label: Have {A_nameDef} help at their hives
li.tip: {A_nameDef} spends a couple of hours beside the beekeepers' hives, learning how they handle them. Practice in animals, and a sting now and then, as at any beehouse.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} will spend a couple of hours at the beekeepers' hives today, learning how they lift the frames without upsetting the bees.
{X_nameDef} has given {A_nameDef} a veil and a smoker, and will show {A_objective} the hives this afternoon.

li.label: Buy a queen from them ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: Once the colony knows how to keep bees, the beekeepers will sell it a young queen of their own, a temperate or a woodland one, carried to the gate in her box.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} took a long look at the colony's beehouses and then at the silver, and picked out one of their young queens. It is being carried to the colony's gate in its box.

texts.li: Mushroom pickers of {FACTION} have come with baskets and a truffle beast on a lead. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} the colony's woods are good ground after the rain, and asked to camp {PLACE} for a few days and pick.

[their:tribal] Cap-gatherers of {FACTION} have come down to the colony's woods with their baskets and a snuffling beast. {X_nameDef} said every cap in the wood has a name, and asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} and gather.

[their:medieval] Truffle hunters of {FACTION} have come up the track with a pig on a rope, which they say is worth more than the cart. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for leave to camp {PLACE} and walk the colony's woods for a few days.

[their:industrial] A family of mushroom pickers from {FACTION} has turned up with folding baskets and a dog that finds truffles. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} and pick the colony's woods while the season lasts.

settled.li: The mushroom pickers' camp {PLACE} is up, with their baskets drying by the fire and the day's caps laid out on the stall.
The pickers from {FACTION} have made camp {PLACE}. Their beast is tied to a stake with its nose in the leaf litter, and their stall already smells of the woods.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the mushroom pickers {PLACE}, says the colony's woods are the best picking {X_pronoun} has had in years, and asks whether there might be a place here for someone who knows them.
{X_nameDef} of the pickers says {X_pronoun} has walked every wood in the region and liked the colony's best, and asks whether there is a place for {X_objective} here.

farewell.li: The mushroom pickers from {FACTION} have gone on with their baskets full and their beast still sniffing.
The pickers' camp {PLACE} is empty, and the woods are quiet again.

lines.li: Never eat one you can't name.
Cut it at the stem and leave the root.
That one's a liar, it only looks like the good one.
Under the old trees, that's where they are.
He's found something, get the trowel.
Don't let him eat it.
Smell that, that's a truffle.
[rain] There'll be more by morning.
[morning] Early, before the slugs get to them.

helpTexts.li: [medicine] {X_nameDef} of the pickers knows healing herbs as well as caps, went out for them at dawn, and has left {COUNT} bundles on the colony's side of their camp.

li.label: Buy a basket of their mushrooms ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: One of the pickers carries a basket of good mushrooms to the colony's gate.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} took the silver and filled a basket, turning every cap over first. One of them is carrying it over to the colony's gate.

li.label: Have {A_nameDef} learn the safe ones with them
li.tip: {A_nameDef} spends a few hours beside the pickers, learning which caps are food and which only look like it. Practice in plants.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} has taken {A_nameDef} aside with a basket of caps, to show {A_objective} the good ones and the liars.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} to see to the one who ate the wrong cap
li.refuseLabel: The pickers can see to their own

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} came to the colony's gate pale and in a hurry: {SICK}, one of the pickers camped {PLACE}, ate a cap that looked right and wasn't, and has been sick since. Would the colony's doctor come?

[their:medieval] {X_nameDef} of the truffle hunters is at the gate. {SICK} tasted one of the caps raw, as they all swear never to do, and has been sick all afternoon. {X_pronoun} asks for the colony's doctor.

li.tip: The colony's doctor walks over to their fire with a medicine and sees to the one who is ill.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} went over to the pickers' camp {PLACE} with the colony's medicine and sat with {SICK} until the worst was over.

refused.li: The pickers nursed {SICK} themselves by the fire, and {X_nameDef} said nothing more about it.

ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.label: hands on the road
ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.leavesWhy: young people walking to a fair carry everything they have on their backs

texts.li: A handful of young people of {FACTION} with bundles on their shoulders have stopped at the colony's land for the night. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they are going to look for places, and asked whether they might camp {PLACE} a night or two. They would work for their supper, {X_pronoun} said, if the colony had any.

[ws:hiring] Young people of {FACTION} walking to {SITUATION} have stopped at the edge of the colony's land. {X_nameDef}, the eldest of them, asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} for a night or two, and said every one of them would work a day for a meal.

[their:medieval] Three or four young people of {FACTION} have stopped at the colony's land on their way to find places, each with the sign of a trade in their hat. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} a night or two, and work for their keep.

[their:industrial] A few young people of {FACTION} with kitbags have stopped at the edge of the colony's land. They are off to look for work, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, and would camp {PLACE} a night or two if the colony let them, and work for their supper.

settled.li: The young people have made camp {PLACE}, a fire and a ring of bundles round it, and somebody is already practising what to say to a master.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the young people camped {PLACE}, came to {A_nameDef} and said {X_pronoun} had stopped looking for a better place than this one. {X_pronoun} asks whether the colony will have {X_objective}.
[ws:hiring] {X_nameDef} of the young people camped {PLACE} has decided {X_pronoun} doesn't need to go on to {SITUATION} after all, if the colony will take {X_objective} on.

farewell.li: The young people have picked up their bundles and gone on down the road to look for places.
[ws:hiring] The young people have gone on toward {SITUATION}, still arguing about who will be hired first.

lines.li: I can drive a cart and mend a fence.
Do you think they'd take me on?
Stand up straight when they look at you.
I'm not going back to my aunt's.
A year's wage and a bed, that's all I want.
Who has the bread?
[their:tribal] The elders will look at our hands first.
[their:industrial] They say the mill pays in coin, not in kind.
[evening] Tomorrow we'll find somewhere, you'll see.

helpTexts.li: [wood] The young people camped {PLACE} cut wood for the colony to show they're worth hiring, and have stacked {COUNT} logs on the colony's side of their fire.

li.label: Give them supper for a day's work
li.tip: A few of the young people fell wood for the colony near their camp, and four of the colony's meals are carried over to their fire for supper.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} had the young people out with axes before the colony's meals had even left the kitchen, and every one of them worked as if a master were watching.
[ws:hiring] The young people went at the colony's wood as if somebody from {SITUATION} were watching them, and {X_nameDef} counted the logs twice to be sure the colony got its supper's worth.
[their:tribal] The young people went out with their axes and their best manners, and brought wood in for the colony's fires before they sat down to eat.

titles.li: [ws:bridge] Carters going the long way round

texts.li: Carters of {FACTION} have brought their beasts up off the road to the colony's land. The road ahead is no good for a loaded cart, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, and they would sooner wait {PLACE} than sit in a ditch. They will sell from their load while they wait.

[ws:mud] Carters of {FACTION} have given up on the road for now: {SITUATION} has swallowed it to the axles. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} until it dries, and said they would sell from their load to pay their way.

[ws:bridge] Carters of {FACTION} going the long way round have stopped at the colony to rest their beasts. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} a couple of days before the next stretch, and said they would trade from their load.

[their:industrial] Carters of {FACTION} have pulled their wagons off the road onto the colony's land. The road ahead is no good for a full load, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, and they would wait {PLACE} a day or two, selling from the wagons while they wait.

settled.li: The carters' camp {PLACE} is up: a fire, their beasts on a line, and their goods stacked under a sheet for anyone who wants to look.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the carters camped {PLACE}, says {X_pronoun} has spent enough of {X_possessive} life waiting for roads to dry, and asks whether the colony could use someone who can drive a team.
{X_nameDef} of the carters says {X_pronoun} has seen enough of the road from a wagon seat, and asks whether the colony could use a steady pair of hands.

farewell.li: The carters from {FACTION} have put their beasts back in the traces and gone on down the road.
[ws:mud] The carters have decided the road is dry enough, or nearly, and set off before anyone could argue.

lines.li: Another day, maybe two.
Feed the beasts before us.
That wheel won't last the season.
I've seen worse roads, not many.
Keep the sheet over the load.
[rain] And there it goes again.
[ws:mud] You could lose a cart in that mud.
[morning] Check the hooves before anything else.
Sell what we can, the load only gets heavier.

momentLines.li: [repair] There, that'll hold until the next town.

helpTexts.li: [mend] {X_nameDef} of the carters had a needle and a strap out anyway, and mended a colonist's worn gear while the beasts rested.

li.label: Send them a hot meal for each of them
li.tip: Hot meals are carried over to the carters' camp from the colony's stores, one each.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is carrying hot meals over to the carters' camp. {X_nameDef} said it was the first warm thing they'd had since the road went bad.

ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.label: gleaners
ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.leavesWhy: gleaners have nothing to leave and carry everything they have

texts.li: A family of {FACTION} with sacks and children has come along the road, looking for fields already harvested. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} a few days and glean what the reapers left, as is the custom where they come from.

[ws:hunger] A family of {FACTION} has come with empty sacks, with {SITUATION} on at home. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef}, not quite meeting {A_possessive} eyes, whether they might camp {PLACE} and glean what the colony's reapers left in the stubble.

[their:tribal] A band of {FACTION} has come with baskets, walking the edges of the land the way their people do after a harvest. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} and gather what was left.

[their:medieval] A family of {FACTION} with sacks over their shoulders has come along the road after the harvest. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} a few days and glean the colony's stubble, as the old custom allows.

settled.li: The gleaners' camp {PLACE} is small: a fire, the sacks, and the children asleep in a heap before it's even dark.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the gleaners camped {PLACE}, asked {A_nameDef} very quietly whether the colony had work for someone who would do anything.
{X_nameDef}, one of the gleaners camped {PLACE}, says the family could manage with one mouth fewer, and asks whether the colony could find work for {X_objective}.

farewell.li: The gleaners have shouldered their sacks, heavier than when they came, and gone on to the next fields.
The gleaners' camp {PLACE} is gone, and there is no trace of it but a ring of ash.

lines.li: Every ear counts.
Stay close where I can see you.
Bend your knees, not your back.
There's a good handful here.
We'll have bread this week.
Say thank you to the lady.
[morning] Out early, before the birds get it.
[child] Can I carry the sack this time?
[evening] Shake out the sacks and see what we have.

helpTexts.li: [wood] The gleaners have cut wood for the colony, {COUNT} logs, stacked on the colony's side of their camp, to say thank you.

li.label: Let them walk the colony's fields
li.refuseLabel: Keep them out of the fields

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} asks whether the gleaners might walk the colony's fields, in the rows already cut, for what the reapers missed. They would not touch a standing plant, {X_pronoun} says.

li.tip: Three of the gleaners walk the colony's fields for a couple of hours, along the rows already cut.

outcomes.li: Three of the gleaners will walk the colony's fields today, bent over the stubble.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} nodded as if {X_pronoun} had expected it, and the gleaners kept to the wild ground.

lines.li: Here's some they missed.
Mind the plants that are still growing.
The colony's reapers are careful, there's not much.

li.label: Send them a sack of food (30 raw food)
li.tip: Thirty raw food is carried over to the gleaners' camp from the colony's stores.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is carrying a sack of food over to the gleaners' camp. {X_nameDef} tried twice to say something and gave up.

titles.li: A games team on the road

texts.li: A team of young people of {FACTION} have stopped on the colony's land to rest their legs on the way to the games. {X_nameDef}, who runs them harder than anyone, asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} and train a day or two.

[ws:games] {FACTION}'s team for {SITUATION} has stopped on the colony's land to rest and train before the last stretch. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for leave to camp {PLACE} a day or two, and said they would be no trouble, which nobody on the team believed.

[their:tribal] Young runners and wrestlers of {FACTION} have stopped at the colony's land on their way to the gathering games. {X_nameDef}, who trains them, asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} and practise for a day or two.

[their:industrial] An athletics team of {FACTION} has stopped on the colony's land to stretch their legs before the meet. {X_nameDef}, their trainer, asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} and train for a day or two.

settled.li: The games team has made camp {PLACE}. Two of them are already racing each other round it, and the rest are pretending not to watch.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef} of the games team camped {PLACE} says {X_pronoun} will never be the region's best, and would sooner be useful somewhere. {X_pronoun} asks whether the colony has a place.
{X_nameDef}, one of the games team, says {X_pronoun} has run enough races for one life, and asks whether the colony could use someone young and quick.

farewell.li: The games team has packed up and gone on toward the games at a jog, because their trainer made them.
[ws:games] The games team has gone on to {SITUATION}, still arguing about who is fastest.

lines.li: Again, from the top.
Your left foot, watch your left foot.
I'll beat you to the tree.
Save it for the day.
Drink some water.
One more lap and then supper.
[their:tribal] The elders will be watching.
[their:medieval] A purse and a garland, think of it.
[their:industrial] Mind your time on the turn.

momentLines.li: [kill] Good shot, that counts as practice.
[kill] That's supper, and good practice for the throw.
[kill] Clean shot, the trainer will be pleased.

helpTexts.li: [meat] The games team brought back more from their hunting than they could eat, and left {COUNT} meat on the colony's side of their camp.

li.label: Have {A_nameDef} train with them
li.tip: {A_nameDef} spends a few hours training beside the games team. Practice in melee.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} has put {A_nameDef} through the team's paces, and will keep at it until {A_pronoun} begs to stop.

ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.label: outlaws walking home
ColonyCouncil.CampKindDef.leavesWhy: people walking home after years away carry what they have left

texts.li: A few worn travelers of {FACTION} have stopped for the night at the edge of the colony's land, on their way home. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, plainly, that they were outlaws until the pardon, and asked whether they might camp {PLACE} a night before the last of the road.

[ws:pardon] Outlaws of {FACTION} walking home under {SITUATION} have stopped at the edge of the colony's land. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for a night's camp {PLACE}, and said they wanted nothing else, which was clearly not quite true.

[their:tribal] A few of {FACTION} who were sent away from their people have stopped at the edge of the colony's land on the way back. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} the elders have called them home, and asked whether they might camp {PLACE} one night.

[their:industrial] A few travelers of {FACTION} with old kitbags have stopped at the edge of the colony's land. They were outlawed once, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} plainly, and the amnesty is taking them home, and they would like to camp {PLACE} for a night.

settled.li: The travelers walking home have made a small fire {PLACE}. They sit close round it and talk about what they will find.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of those camped {PLACE} on the way home, says there is nobody left at home for {X_objective} after all these years, and asks whether the colony would take {X_objective} instead.
{X_nameDef} of those walking home says {X_pronoun} is not sure there is still a home to go to, and asks whether the colony would let {X_objective} stay instead.

farewell.li: The travelers walking home have gone on at first light, faster than they came.
The camp {PLACE} is empty. They left early, to be home before dark.

lines.li: Do you think they'll know me?
Eleven years, it's been.
Nobody will say anything, it's a pardon.
My mother will still be cross.
One more day's walk.
I wonder if the old mill's still there.
[evening] Last night on the road, I hope.
I hope someone still keeps my seat at the table.
[morning] Up and walking, we're nearly there.

momentLines.li: [carry,wood] Last of the wood for tonight.

helpTexts.li: [wood] Those camped {PLACE} on the way home cut wood for the colony, {COUNT} logs, and stacked it on the colony's side of their camp to pay for the night.

li.label: Send them food for the road (20 raw food)
li.tip: Twenty raw food is carried over to their camp from the colony's stores, for the last of the road.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is carrying food over to the travelers' camp for the last of their road. {X_nameDef} said they would tell their people at home where it came from.

texts.li: Star-watchers of {FACTION} have come with their charts and a lot of blankets. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} the colony's land has a clear, dark sky, and asked to camp {PLACE} a few nights and watch it.

[ws:stars] Star-watchers of {FACTION} have come for the falling stars, with charts, a lantern with a red cloth over it and very little sleep between them. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for leave to camp {PLACE}, where the sky is dark, and watch through the nights.
[ws:comet] Watchers of {FACTION} have come out to see {SITUATION} away from the lights of the towns. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} a few nights and mark its path.

[their:tribal] Sky-readers of {FACTION} have come to the colony's land to lie on their backs under its sky. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} the stars here are close, and asked to camp {PLACE} a few nights.

settled.li: The star-watchers' camp {PLACE} is up, with their blankets laid out on the open ground and their charts weighted down with stones.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the star-watchers {PLACE}, says {X_pronoun} has never seen a sky like the colony's, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay under it for good.
{X_nameDef} of the star-watchers says the nights here are darker and clearer than anywhere in the region, and asks whether the colony would have someone who watches them.

farewell.li: The star-watchers from {FACTION} have rolled up their charts and gone, yawning, in the middle of the day.
[ws:stars] The star-watchers have gone home with a book full of falling stars, and say the colony's sky was the best they had.

lines.li: There, did you see it?
Mark the time.
Keep the lantern covered.
That one's been there all night.
Clear tonight, we're lucky.
[ws:stars] That's forty since dusk.
[ws:comet] It's moved since last night.
[rain] No sky tonight, then.
[night] Look up, and give your eyes a while.

helpTexts.li: [mend] {X_nameDef} of the star-watchers had nothing to do in the daylight, and spent an hour of it mending a colonist's worn gear.

li.label: Have {A_nameDef} watch the sky with them tonight
li.tip: {A_nameDef} goes over to the star-watchers' camp in the evening and sits with them a while. Practice in intellectual.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is going over to the star-watchers' camp this evening, to lie on a blanket and learn the names they have for the stars.
